issues.title: Generic calendar suffix filtering includes disabled providers
issues.description: The getGenericCalendarSuffixes() method uses Object.keys(GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES) to iterate over all providers defined in the constant, including office365_calendar. However, getProviders() only returns ['google_calendar'], meaning Office365 is not actually enabled. This causes the subscription system to filter out Office365 calendar suffixes even when Office365 calendars shouldn't be processed at all. The filtering should only include suffixes for enabled providers by using this.getProviders() as in the original implementation.

issues.title: Empty suffix array incorrectly bypasses generic calendar filtering
issues.description: The filtering logic adds a length check (genericCalendarSuffixes?.length) that treats an empty array as falsy, setting AND to undefined instead of an empty array. In Prisma, AND: undefined means no filtering, while AND: [] also means no filtering but with different semantics. More critically, this breaks the filtering for providers like office365_calendar that have an empty suffix list in GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES. The double optional chaining (?. used twice) is redundant and the length check changes the behavior from the intended design where empty arrays should still be processed.

issues.title: Incomplete class rename breaks all imports and causes runtime failures
issues.description: The class was renamed from SelectedCalendarRepository to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository (line 5) without providing a backward-compatible export alias. This breaks all existing code that imports this class. The test file within this PR (SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts:2,50,53) still imports and instantiates the old class name, causing test failures. Production code in apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts:41 and apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts:61 also use 'new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)' which will fail at runtime with a TypeError indicating SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26774 - feat: CalendarCache - filter generic calendars from subscription batch

structured_output.summary:
The PR stops calendar subscription sync from picking up Google's generic calendars (holidays, shared, imported, resource calendars) by filtering on externalId suffixes. A `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` map is added to `AdaptersFactory.ts`, exposed through a new `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` method, passed by `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions` into `findNextSubscriptionBatch`, and turned into a Prisma `AND: [{ NOT: { externalId: { endsWith } } }]` clause. The suffix list and the Prisma filter are sound: `externalId` is a non-null `String` in the schema, so `NOT`/`endsWith` cannot hit NULL semantics.

However, the PR renames the class `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository` in `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` without updating its importers. The two cron/webhook routes that construct it (`apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts`) and the repository's own test file still import `SelectedCalendarRepository`, so they break at build time and at runtime. The new filter also applies Google's suffixes to every integration in the batch, which discards the per-provider structure of the map.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The class rename is a build- and runtime-breaking change. `new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)` in the cron and webhook routes will fail once the export no longer exists, and the repository test file cannot import its subject, so the new filter tests never run. Once the rename is reverted or all importers are updated, the core filter logic looks correct and the remaining items are medium or low.

architecture.overview:
Calendar subscription sync is driven by `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions`, which is invoked from the cron route at `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` and from the webhook route. It pulls a batch of `SelectedCalendar` rows that still need a subscription, using `SelectedCalendarRepository.findNextSubscriptionBatch` (a Prisma `findMany`), and then subscribes each one through the provider adapter returned by `DefaultAdapterFactory`.

This PR adds a second filter to that batch query. `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` declares which externalId suffixes belong to Google's non-personal calendars. `AdapterFactory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` flattens those lists across providers, and the service forwards them as `genericCalendarSuffixes`, which the repository turns into `AND: [NOT endsWith]` conditions. The PR also renames the repository class, which is the one change that touches existing wiring.
steps: Entry point: the cron route and webhook route construct `CalendarSubscriptionService` with `DefaultAdapterFactory` and a `SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)` instance imported from the feature path.
`checkForNewSubscriptions` calls `findNextSubscriptionBatch` with `integrations` from `getProviders()`, `teamIds`, and now `genericCalendarSuffixes` from `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()`.
`GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` in `AdaptersFactory.ts` is the new source of truth, keyed by provider. `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` flattens it into one list, with no provider scoping.
`PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository.findNextSubscriptionBatch` adds one `NOT endsWith` clause per suffix inside `where.AND`, leaving the existing integration, OR, and team filters unchanged.
The rename from `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository` breaks every importer that still uses the old name, including the two routes above and the repository test.

findings.title: Class rename breaks existing importers and the repository test
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` line 5, the class was renamed to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, which breaks existing imports. Revert the class name to `SelectedCalendarRepository`. If the rename is intentional, update every importer in the same change instead: `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts` (line 11, 41), `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts` (line 14, 61), and `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts` (lines 3 and 53). Then grep the repo for the old import path to confirm nothing else depends on the old name.

findings.title: Google suffixes are applied to all providers, discarding the per-provider map
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts` lines 67-70, `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` flattens the per-provider `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` map into one list, so Google suffixes are applied to every integration in the batch. Decide whether the filter is meant to be global or provider-scoped. If global, rename the method and the constant to reflect that. If provider-scoped, change the repository's `genericCalendarSuffixes` parameter in `SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` (lines 27 and 41-45) to a per-integration mapping and build the `AND` clause per integration. Keep the existing `NOT endsWith` shape.

findings.title: Suffix filter is opt-in and fails open when the argument is omitted
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` (lines 27 and 41-45) and the matching interface in `SelectedCalendarRepository.interface.ts` (line 35), `genericCalendarSuffixes` is optional, so omitting it silently disables the generic-calendar filter. Make the parameter required in both the interface and the implementation so that the compiler catches any caller that omits it. Update the cron route and webhook route constructors and the tests to pass the suffixes explicitly. Keep the `NOT endsWith` clause shape unchanged.

findings.title: AdapterFactory tests do not cover the new method or the suffix list
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests in `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/__tests__/AdaptersFactory.test.ts` for `DefaultAdapterFactory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()`. Assert that the result contains the four Google suffixes (`@group.v.calendar.google.com`, `@group.calendar.google.com`, `@import.calendar.google.com`, `@resource.calendar.google.com`) and nothing from `office365_calendar`. In `CalendarSubscriptionService.test.ts`, replace the four duplicated hard-coded suffix literals with a reference to the exported `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` from `AdaptersFactory.ts` so that the tests track the real list.

findings.title: Redundant optional chaining in the suffix mapping
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` lines 41-45, remove the unnecessary `?.` in `genericCalendarSuffixes?.map` because the preceding `?.length` truthiness check already narrows the value. Keep the rest of the expression unchanged.

findings.title: Prisma NOT/endsWith is safe because externalId is non-null
Suffix list matches Google's generic calendar domains
findings.body:
The four Google suffixes (`@group.v.calendar.google.com` for holidays, `@group.calendar.google.com` for shared calendars, `@import.calendar.google.com` for imported calendars, and `@resource.calendar.google.com` for resource calendars) identify the non-personal calendar types the PR describes. A user's primary calendar externalId is their account email, so personal calendars are not affected.
